description: Original synthetic archive fixtures for independent #39/#61 preparation.

verification.notes: Python stdlib validates container decoding and intended malformed byte structures only; no docsluice extraction was run.

known_gaps: No true ZIP quine fixture is included. A recursive ZIP containing itself was not constructed or verified.
The nested amplification inputs are deliberately bounded and do not represent gigabyte-scale expansion.
Malformed TAR cases assert header/body contradictions; expected docsluice reader outcomes remain unverified.

fixtures.notes: #39 valid mixed archive: ordered CSV, HTML, nested ZIP, original 1x1 RGBA PNG, directory.
#39 names test path traversal and common macOS/Windows OS junk; no extraction is performed.
#39 exactly 10,000 empty ZIP entries, stored without compression.
#39 bounded four-container nesting around about 512 KiB of repeated leaf data; not a dangerous-scale bomb.
#61 single-member gzip containing a small CSV.
#61 two concatenated gzip members; standard-library decompression yields both in order.
#61 gzip FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT, and FHCRC fields.
#61 bounded 512 KiB repeated data for decompression-ratio testing.
#61 ustar nested folders, regular CSV, and a symlink listed as metadata; no link traversal.
#61 valid PAX extended path record with a 65,536-character component, bounded metadata stress.
#61 GNU long-name extension for a 180-character path.
#61 malformed ustar header with first name byte flipped after checksum creation.
#61 malformed ustar header claims a 1,000,000-byte regular file but provides five body bytes.
#61 malformed PAX extended header claims a 1,000,000-byte metadata body but provides one 10-byte path record.
#61 gzip-compressed ustar archive containing nested folders, CSV, and symlink metadata.
